sections.title: Percentage Fundamentals
sections.description: Build a clear understanding of percentage and its basic representations.

concepts.title: Meaning of Percentage
concepts.shortDescription: Understand percentage as a fraction out of 100.

blocks.title: Definition
blocks.value: Percentage means a quantity expressed per hundred.
The symbol % means 'per hundred'. Therefore, 25% means 25 out of 100.

concepts.title: Converting a Fraction to Percentage
concepts.shortDescription: Convert a fraction into percentage form.

blocks.value: To convert a fraction into percentage, multiply the fraction by 100.

blocks.title: Competitive Shortcut
blocks.value: For common fractions, memorize their percentage equivalents.

sections.title: Percentage Increase and Decrease
sections.description: Understand how percentage change is calculated and applied.

concepts.title: Percentage Increase
concepts.shortDescription: Calculate the percentage increase from an original value.

blocks.title: Percentage Increase
blocks.value: Percentage increase measures how much a quantity has increased relative to its original value.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.value: The denominator for percentage increase is the original value.

concepts.title: Percentage Decrease
concepts.shortDescription: Calculate the percentage decrease from an original value.

blocks.title: Percentage Decrease
blocks.value: Percentage decrease measures how much a quantity has decreased relative to its original value.

blocks.title: Common Mistake
blocks.value: Do not use the final value as the denominator when calculating percentage decrease.

sections.title: Advanced Percentage
sections.description: Develop competitive-exam skills involving successive and reverse percentage changes.

concepts.title: Successive Percentage Change
concepts.shortDescription: Handle two or more successive percentage increases or decreases.

blocks.value: Successive percentage changes occur when a quantity is changed by a percentage and then changed again using the new value.

blocks.title: Important
blocks.value: The second percentage is applied to the changed value, not the original value.

blocks.title: Exam Shortcut
blocks.value: For successive percentage changes, use the direct net-change formula whenever applicable.

concepts.title: Reverse Percentage
concepts.shortDescription: Find the original quantity when the final quantity and percentage change are known.

blocks.title: Reverse Percentage
blocks.value: Reverse percentage problems require finding the original value from a value obtained after a percentage change.

blocks.title: Common Mistake
blocks.value: A percentage increase and the corresponding reverse percentage decrease are generally not equal.
